reason: LLM-as-a-judge Bedrock model evaluation with a custom prompt dataset and chosen dimensions is the scalable automated fit. Human eval is not scalable, BERTScore/F1 needs gold references and the claim it fully captures faithfulness is false, and a length alarm measures nothing.

High context relevance plus low groundedness means the generator adds content unsupported by retrieved passages. Options 0 and 3 contradict the stated high context relevance, and option 2 contradicts the acceptable answer relevance.

A Bedrock guardrail contextual grounding check scores grounding and relevance against thresholds and blocks ungrounded responses at inference. Raising temperature worsens hallucination, few-shot cannot deterministically block, and no larger model eliminates hallucination.

ThrottlingException at peak calls for backoff with jitter plus a quota increase or Provisioned Throughput. Missing IAM permission yields AccessDeniedException on every call, max_tokens relates to ValidationException, and logging does not retry.

With IAM allowing InvokeModel and other models working, a new model failing AccessDeniedException means model access was not granted for that model in the account and Region, a step separate from IAM. Quota gives ThrottlingException and schema or length gives ValidationException.

A canary or A-B deployment routes a small slice of live traffic and compares quality and business metrics against the current prompt, limiting blast radius. 100 percent cutover maximizes risk, more offline eval never touches production, and Provisioned Throughput addresses latency not quality.

Bedrock model invocation logging captures full prompt and completion payloads to S3 and CloudWatch Logs, and CloudWatch alarms on InvocationLatency and InvocationServerErrors provide threshold alerting. CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and X-Ray do not persist model input and output bodies.
